newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO PROBE PRIVATISATION CONSULTANCY FEES.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO PROBE PRIVATISATION CONSULTANCY FEES.

text.p: Hungary's minister in charge of privatisation agrees with the Prime Minister's Monday decision to investigate consultancy contracts for fees an opposition party said are exagerated.

"Not only do I agree with the Prime Minister's decision but I also took steps to speed up the investigation," Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman, who is also in charge of Hungary's privatisation, told reporters on Monday.

Opposition party Young Democrats (FIDESZ-MPP) on Saturday asked for Suchman's resignation following reports that the state privatisation agency APV Rt paid 300 million forints to Marta Tocsik for negotiating on its behalf.

Prime Minister Gyula Horn told Monday in parliament he had instructed the Government Supervision Office to investigate the consultancy contracts and report the results in time for the October 4 cabinet meeting.
Suchman also said he did not know of the contract and while not wanting to anticipate the outcome of the inquiry, he considered the contract unethical.

Suchman, a member of the ruling Socialst party, previously minister without protfolio in charge of privatisation, took over on September 1 the helm of the Industry and Trade Ministry from Imre Dunai, who resigned quoting health reasons.
Parallel with his nomination, the government has put the supervision of the privatisation process under the Industry and Trade Ministry.
